to live a life in accordance with the beatitudes. today, we really stand on the shoulders of giants. over the last two thousand years countless men, women and children of many eras, places and cultures have spent their lives in the service of the good news of jesus christ. from among these many, a smaller group of individuals have earned the distinction of being known as “saints.” these are real people to whom we look for example. these are real people to whom we look for inspiration. these are real people to whom we look for encouragement and grace. these saints - these real people - have blazed a trail amid challenges and trials while living and proclaiming the gospel. the challenge for us is to follow their example in ways that fit the state and stage of life in which we find ourselves. francis de sales wrote: “look at the example given by the saints in every walk of life. there is nothing that they have not done in order to love god and to be god's devoted followers. why then should we not do as much according to our position and vocation in life to keep the cherished resolution and holy protestations that we have made?” so, what does it mean to be a saint? surprisingly, it is much more down-to- earth and obtainable than we might think. francis de sales observed: “we must love all that god loves, and god loves our vocation; so let us love our vocation, too, and not waste our energy hankering after a different sort of life, but get on with your ownjob. be martha as well as mary, and be both gladly, faithfully doing what you are called to do.” in the view of st. francis de sales, sanctity - sainthood - is measured by our willingness and ability to embrace the state and stage of life in which we find ourselves. saints are people who deeply embraced their lives as they found them, rather than wasting time wishing or waiting for an opportunity to live someone else's life. sainthood - sanctity - holiness - is marked by the willingness to embrace god's will as it is manifested in the ups and downs of everyday life. so how are we being called to be saints? and how in the midst of our trials, might we blaze a trail of love for just today?

during this month of november, we pray especially for our brothers and sisters wh o have died. we pray that they have passed from death to life in the company of the lord jesus , who died and rose to new life. we dedicate the month of november to their memory and commend them to the love and mercy of go d, our father. we also pray for those who mourn the death of a loved one. in our darkest moments, the risen christ is among us to bring new light and hope. lord of all gent leness, surround us with your care and comfort us in our sorrow. it is our c ertain faith that your son jesus christ, who died on the cross was raised from the dead. grant through this mystery, that all who to their eternal rest in christ may now sh are in the joy of his resurrection. we ask this through christ our lord. amen. november: the month of the holy souls. join us for a triduum of masses for the dead in clara church. tuesday 10th november 7:30pm: for all deceased parents & grandparents. wednesday 11th november 7:30pm: for children & all who died young. thursday 12th november 7:30pm: for those who died tragically, in war or by suicide. may their gentle souls rest in peace. ‘ní imithe uainn atá siad, ach imithe romhainn’.
